What I Want To Acheive This Block (& How?):

-> Manage the relationship between educational research and ‘job’ research
> Can I have a work-life balance between professional and educational requirements?

Implement better use of personal calendar. Fill in 'softer' things like personal relaxing time, and time with friends (& cats). Write a "priority list" so that if I get too busy on a particular period, I know what is safe to temporarily pause/drop from my schedule. Importantly; plan towards the end of this semester make sure to plan the methodology section in an efficient manner. Implement practical ways to do research that don't require extensive time-usage, and/or can be spread out thinly over many weeks.

Deadline & Presentations

^ note: record internal vs external influence factors.

Progress:
-> Created a flexible & easily maintainable tagging system for my Zotero sources database.
-> Figured out the Zotero API, so that I can batch-tag and batch process PDFs where necessary.
-> Asked Claude to make a simple visual graph of the sources publication timeline, citation interlinking, and tag linking.
-> Made a further graph that uses force-lines to visualise research gaps (and/or lack of source collection) between database sources. This way Claude is only used to create the visual; the tags and citation information does the rest of the work.
-> These graphs can then be used as a ‘literature process report’ across this semester, by simply exporting the graph at any point in time.
Research Source Graphs:

^ First research paper pass. Includes Foundational papers like Osrtom’s ‘Governing The Commons’, as well as her lectures on ‘Collective Action’. The right-side blob are all to do with Machine-Learning maps. No research connects the two subjects yet.

^ Second research paper pass. Includes more of Ostrom’s work across 1970-2009, as well as more recent additional papers that directly cite many of her works (such as ‘Institutional navigation for polycentric sustainability governance’). Also included in this pass are further ML papers and several research projects I have personal connection to. These can be seen as the grey dots floating inbetween the two separate research areas.

^ Third research paper pass. On this one I focused on papers directly relating to Ostrom’s work; especially more recent papers that actually take her work out of theory and into real practice. This revealed some Contrarian sources; especially around how the Commons theories treat power dynamics, and the lack of long-term behavioural studies on Commons-in-practice (e.g. ‘The black box of power in polycentric environmental governance’). One especially useful connectuve paper popped-up; ‘Smart Earth: A meta-review and implications for environmental governance’ - which will likely be useful in bridging the gap between the social and technical themes in my project.
Reflection:
-> I think the solution I found for Claude to make graphs, while I provide the citation information and tags, is a neat empirical solution to evaluating ‘research gaps’.
-> Stating the above; I do have to take my research visualisation with a pinch of salt, as the information/pattern output is only as good as the tags I provide.
-> My research is heavily leaning into the socio-economic theory; as research papers are much easier to find for that area. The theory is older, there is an active discussion since the 1960’s about the ‘Commons’ topic, and every paper tends to cite each other (making it very easy to evaluate argument patterns across multiple papers). However the more technical ‘Machine-Learning’ side is newer; which means fewer papers, fewer cross-citations (multiple papers coming out simultaneously don’t tend to cite each other), and similar problem ‘themes’ are often are solved with solutions where the technical stack is different.
Action Points
-> Start exporting my ‘research graphs’ and placing them in the learning logs dedicated section.
-> Look further out than research papers (blogs, github, etc) for information about Machine Learning, Embedding model application, and using ML in maps.

Risks & Mitigations:
-> risk There may be no discernable links between the map-machine-learning and the socio-economic theory of the Commons. mitigation If this ends up being the case, then use the literature review to explain this gap and why it makes my research particularly poignant.
-> risk As my work becomes more and more socio-economic focused, it is clearer that the eventual methodology will require qualitative data with groups of people. mitigation Use BUAS & DAE students for this, and plan well in advance. Note in the methodology (& presentations) that this was the approach due to time constraints, and show the intended ‘target audience’ if I had unlimited time and money.
^ note: record both risk factors and their related  mitigation plan.

Extra ILO’s:

^ Planning my Introduction to 3D class. For Design Academy Eindhoven 4th year students, this is a 6-day class that goes through 3D concepts, introduction to networked systems, microcontrollers into 3D editors, and environment building in Blender.
